summary: George Berrington reviewed six recent proposals with Paul and Rebecca. Proposals offer both gain-share and fixed fee without a recommendation, and procurement teams use that to stall. We agreed a single recommended fee option and a clearer qualification step.

discussion.keyPoints: Four of six proposals listed two fee options side by side. Rebecca said clients spent weeks comparing them and two went quiet.
Paul tends to discount fixed fees by 10% to 15% at the end. Rebecca thinks this signals the price was padded.
Thornbury often scopes before confirming the CFO is sponsoring the project, so procurement managers block it.

recommendations.recommendation: Present one recommended fee option: gain-share at 25% of verified first-year savings for engagements with spend over £40m.
No discounting on fixed fees; trade scope instead, such as removing a category.
Confirm CFO sponsorship in writing before any scoping work starts.
Prepare a one-page answer to the 'we already have a procurement team' objection.

actions.action: Rewrite the proposal template with a single fee recommendation

nextFocus: Define pipeline stages and conversion targets.
nextPreparation: Rebecca to export all open opportunities with stage and expected fee.

tests.question: What fee option do our proposals recommend?
Is written CFO sponsorship before scoping agreed?
What did we agree about discounting?
